scope: presentation-only audio (cannot read or change a result, payout or timing)
originality: All music and effects are original, composed as note data and synthesised in code (no samples, no downloaded assets, no third-party melodies or motifs). Outbound asset sites were blocked; no licences were bought.

method.harness: Headless Chromium renders every asset with the production code path (Web Worker synthesis + OfflineAudioContext reverb + JS mastering), then measures the float output in the page and exports 16-bit WAVs (TPDF dither).
method.loudness: ITU-R BS.1770 K-weighting, 400 ms blocks / 75 % overlap, absolute (−70 LUFS) and relative (−10 LU) gates; momentary = max 400 ms block; short-term = max 3 s window.
method.spectrum: 4096-point Hann FFT averaged over ≤160 frames of the mid signal; centroid of the power spectrum; band energy relative to total.
method.seam: step from the last to the first sample vs. every sample-to-sample step of the loop (median, 99.9th percentile, max, percentile rank); RMS of 50 ms each side.
method.runtimeChain: base theme through the real bus graph (trim → glue compressor → limiter) in an OfflineAudioContext, alone and under a worst-case stack of 40 effects plus a big-win stinger with a −14 dB duck.

environment.machine: cloud container, 4 vCPU Intel Xeon 2.8 GHz (2 physical cores with HT behaviour); another agent ran Chromium tests and a next dev server concurrently (load average ≈ 6), so timings are pessimistic and noisy

targets.harshness: little energy above 8 kHz, bells capped at 9 kHz partials
targets.loopSeam: seam step must be an ordinary step of the music
targets.loadTime: core (base theme + base-game effects) ≲ 3 s on a desktop; the rest lazily

renderTiming.note: core = base theme + base-game effects (what play needs); the feature theme, idle, ambience, stingers, beds and feature effects render afterwards in the background. Before core is ready a live-synth fallback answers every call.
renderTiming.workerPathVerified: next dev (Turbopack) /lab/audio: 3 module workers, 64 jobs, no inline fallback

limitations: Nobody has listened to this audio: the author cannot hear. Musical quality, mix balance and "commercial-slot" feel need the owner's listening acceptance (WAVs below).
Loudness, peaks, spectra and seams are measured; taste is not. Stem balance is set by per-stem loudness targets, not by ear.

Load times were measured in a loaded 4-vCPU cloud container, not on a desktop or a phone; no mobile CPU or memory measurement (decoded buffers ≈ 87 MB at 44.1 kHz stereo float: 173 s of music + 74.5 s of effects (89 clips); createCascadeSound({ sampleRate: 32000 }) would cut this to ≈ 63 MB).

The bus limiter is the browser DynamicsCompressor (6 ms look-ahead, not a true brickwall); the stress test stays below −1 dBTP but other browsers may differ (Safari/Firefox compressors were not measured).
Reverb runs at half rate (22.05 kHz) for speed; its tail is band-limited by design.

v3.scope: Candy Cascade sound set v3: win-tier escalation (Büyük/Mega/Süper/Efsane + max win), tier-up transitions, per-tier count-up beds and landings, multiplier callouts (6 classes, voice-line slot), total-win fanfare. Presentation only.
v3.originality: All new music and effects are original note data and code synthesis (wordless formant choir, modal tower bells, formant "vox" and brass-like stabs are new instruments written for this set). No samples, no voice recordings, no third-party melodies or motifs; the vox is non-verbal by design.

environment.machine: cloud container, 4 vCPU; other agents ran a next dev server and Chromium concurrently (load average 8–14 during these runs), so timings are pessimistic and noisy

v3.method: Same harness as the top-level measurements: headless Chromium, production code path (Web Worker synthesis via the prebuilt worker bundle + OfflineAudioContext reverb + JS mastering), BS.1770 loudness, 4× true peak, seam statistic; 16-bit TPDF WAV export. The escalation runs replay the runtime schedule (planTierUp) through the real bus graph (buildBusGraph) at the default mix with the base scene under a −20 dB duck.

escalation.note: Count-up from Büyük to Efsane (and on to max win): head 1, bed 1 on its musical end, tier-up calls at 5.3 / 8.15 / 10.7 (/ 13.25) s, landing when the count stops. hits: every hit lands on the 120 BPM grid; callToHitMs is the delay from the bigWin() call. The largest sample steps right before a hit come from the coin ticks and the rising whoosh (content): with both removed (cutIsolation) the 80–100 ms cut fades rank at the 78–94th percentile of all steps, i.e. no click.
